# Touying: complete reference for LLM agents

> Touying is a Typst package for presentation slides (like LaTeX Beamer). This file is everything an agent needs to
> write a correct deck: the document skeleton, slides and themes, animations, configuration, output modes, and the
> manim-style scene system (`touying-scene`) for animated maths, graphs and 3D, exported to a self-contained HTML
> file by touying-exporter.
>
> Every complete example in this file compiles with Typst 0.15. When in doubt, compile and look at the pages.

Contents:
1. Rules that prevent most errors
2. Skeleton
3. Slides and structure
4. Themes
5. Step-by-step reveals (subslides)
6. Configuration
7. Speaker notes, output modes, handouts
8. Scenes: manim-style animation
9. Scenes: graphs
10. Scenes: morphing
11. Scenes: emphasis and annotations
12. Scenes: 3D
13. HTML export
14. Errors and fixes
15. Checklist before handing a deck over

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Rules that prevent most errors

1. Import, then apply a theme with a show rule, then write content:
   `#import "@preview/touying:0.8.1": *`, `#import themes.simple: *`, `#show: simple-theme.with(..)`.
2. Headings create slides. With most themes `= Section` starts a section and `== Title` starts a slide. Text
   before the first heading after the show rule lands on an untitled slide.
3. All configuration goes into the theme call as `config-*(..)` arguments:
   `#show: metropolis-theme.with(aspect-ratio: "16-9", config-info(title: [..]), config-common(..))`.
4. `#pause` and `#meanwhile` are markers in the slide body. They do not work inside `context`, inside layout
   functions such as `grid` cells, or inside function calls that are not touying-aware. Use the callback style there
   (section 5).
5. Scenes (`touying-scene`) are in the development version of touying (branch `feature/animations`), not yet in
   `@preview/touying:0.8.1`. Import that checkout by path:
   `#import "/lib.typ": *` (compile with `--root` at the checkout) or `#import "path/to/touying/lib.typ": *`.
6. Typst has no duration type: times in scenes are plain numbers of seconds. Scene coordinates are plain numbers
   (y up); lengths such as `1cm` are layout distances from the scene's top-left corner (y down).
7. Object names in scenes may only contain letters, digits, `-` and `_`.
8. Compile to check: `typst compile slides.typ` (add `--root <dir>` when importing by absolute path), and render a
   few pages to PNG to look at them: `typst compile slides.typ "page-{p}.png" --ppi 60`.

## 2. Skeleton

```typst
#import "@preview/touying:0.8.1": *
#import themes.metropolis: *

#show: metropolis-theme.with(
  aspect-ratio: "16-9",
  config-info(
    title: [Measuring the Hubble Constant],
    subtitle: [With gravitational lensing],
    author: [A. Author],
    date: datetime.today(),
    institution: [Some University],
  ),
)

#title-slide()

= Introduction

== Motivation

- Tension between early- and late-universe measurements.
- #pause A third method helps.

== The key equation

$ H_0 = v / d $

#focus-slide[Questions?]
```

## 3. Slides and structure

- `= Heading` (level 1) is a section. Most themes show a section slide automatically.
- `== Heading` (level 2) is a slide title, and the content until the next heading is that slide.
- `config-common(slide-level: n)` sets how many heading levels create slides (default 2; dewdrop uses 3).
- `#slide[..]` creates a slide explicitly; `#slide(title: [..])[..]` is not portable across themes, so prefer
  headings for titles.
- `#pagebreak()` or a bare `---` line starts a new slide with the same title.
- Heading labels: `<touying:hidden>` (no section slide, unnumbered, not in the outline), `<touying:skip>` (no section
  slide), `<touying:unnumbered>`, `<touying:unoutlined>`, `<touying:unbookmarked>`, `<touying:handout>` (slide only
  in handouts).
- Outline: `#components.adaptive-columns(outline(title: none, indent: 1em))`, or `#outline-slide()` in themes that
  have it.
- Numbering: `#set heading(numbering: "1.1")`.
- Columns: `#cols[left][right]` or `#cols(columns: (2fr, 1fr), gutter: 1em)[..][..]`. `side-by-side` is an alias.
- `#alert[..]` emphasises text in the theme's colour.
- `#show: appendix` before the appendix section freezes the slide counter.
- Multi-file decks: `#include "part.typ"` works; each included file needs `#import "@preview/touying:0.8.1": *` if it
  uses touying functions.

## 4. Themes

Import with `#import themes.<name>: *` and apply with `#show: <name>-theme.with(aspect-ratio: "16-9", ..)`.

| Theme | Slide functions | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `simple` | `title-slide[body]`, `centered-slide[..]`, `focus-slide[..]`, `new-section-slide` | `title-slide` takes its content as body. |
| `metropolis` | `title-slide()`, `outline-slide()`, `focus-slide[..]`, `new-section-slide` | Uses `config-info`. Options: `footer:`, `footer-progress:`, `header-right:`. |
| `dewdrop` | `title-slide()`, `outline-slide()`, `focus-slide[..]` | `slide-level` 3; navigation bar via `navigation:`. |
| `university` | `title-slide()`, `focus-slide[..]`, `matrix-slide[..][..]` | Uses `config-info` including `institution`, `logo`. |
| `aqua` | `title-slide()`, `outline-slide()`, `focus-slide[..]` | |
| `stargazer` | `title-slide()`, `outline-slide()`, `focus-slide[..]`, `ending-slide[..]`, `tblock(title:)[..]` | |

`config-info(title:, subtitle:, author:, date:, institution:, contact:, logo:, extra:)` feeds the title slide,
header and footer of every theme. `aspect-ratio` is `"16-9"` or `"4-3"`. Global styles go after the theme's show
rule, e.g. `#set text(font: "Fira Sans")`.

## 5. Step-by-step reveals (subslides)

One slide can produce several pages ("subslides") that reveal content step by step.

```typst
#import "@preview/touying:0.8.1": *
#import themes.simple: *
#show: simple-theme.with(aspect-ratio: "16-9")

== Markers

First #pause second, on page 2.

#pause

Third, on page 3.

#meanwhile

Shown from page 1 alongside "First"; #pause this from page 2.

== Functions

#uncover("2-")[Visible from page 2; space reserved before.]

#only("2-")[Visible from page 2; no space reserved before.]

#alternatives[first version][second version]

$
  f(x) &= pause x^2 + 2x + 1 \
       &= pause (x + 1)^2
$

== Callback style

#slide(repeat: 3, self => [
  #let (uncover, only, alternatives) = utils.methods(self)
  Page #self.subslide of 3. #uncover("3")[Only on page 3.]
])
```

- Index syntax: `2`, `"2-"`, `"-3"`, `"1, 3-4"`, or an array `(1, 3)`.
- `#pause` inside an equation works (shown above).
- CeTZ and fletcher drawings animate with `touying-reduce`: `#let cetz-canvas = touying-reduce.with(cetz)`, then
  inside the drawing use `(pause,)` between commands. For fletcher, `#let diagram = touying-reduce.with(fletcher)` and
  plain `pause` between `node`/`edge` arguments.
- The callback style (`slide(repeat: n, self => ..)` with `utils.methods(self)`) works where markers do not, e.g.
  inside `grid`, `table` or `context`.
- Covered content is hidden by default. Show it dimmed instead with
  `config-methods(cover: utils.semi-transparent-cover)` or `utils.alpha-changing-cover`.

## 6. Configuration

All `config-*` functions are passed to the theme call and merged.

| Function | Important keys |
| --- | --- |
| `config-info` | `title`, `subtitle`, `author`, `date`, `institution`, `contact`, `logo`, `extra` |
| `config-common` | `slide-level`, `handout`, `handout-subslides`, `export-mode`, `show-notes-on-second-screen`, `show-only-notes`, `frozen-counters`, `datetime-format` |
| `config-page` | `paper`, `margin`, `header`, `footer`, `fill`, `background` (like `set page`) |
| `config-colors` | `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `neutral-lightest`, ... |
| `config-methods` | `cover`, `init`, `alert` |
| `config-scene` | `run-time`, `rate`, `samples-per-second`, `max-samples`, `max-geometry` (scenes, section 8) |

Example: `#show: university-theme.with(aspect-ratio: "16-9", config-colors(primary: rgb("#04364A")))`.

## 7. Speaker notes, output modes, handouts

- `#speaker-note[..]` on a slide. Notes go to the pdfpc file by default, to a second screen with
  `config-common(show-notes-on-second-screen: right)`, and to the HTML presenter window (section 13).
- Output modes: `config-common(export-mode: "presentation" | "handout" | "slides" | "article")` or
  `--input export-mode=handout` on the command line.
- Handouts keep the last subslide of each slide by default; `config-common(handout-subslides: 1)` or `(1, -1)` or
  `"1-2"` chooses others.
- Mode-specific content: `#presentation-only[..]`, `#handout-only[..]`, `#slides-only[..]`, `#article-only[..]`,
  `#article-text[..]` (replaces the slide in article mode).

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 8. Scenes: manim-style animation

`touying-scene` animates named objects along a timeline, like manim. The same source gives:

- **PDF, handout and article:** one page per `click`, showing the state at the end of that step. These are ordinary
  subslides.
- **HTML:** a self-contained file in which everything actually moves: fades, drawing, writing, morphs, trackers,
  graphs and 3D. It is exported with touying-exporter (section 13).

Mental model:
- `objects` is a dictionary of named things to draw.
- `timeline` is an array of steps. A bare animation is one step; `play(..)` runs several together; `wait(s)` pauses;
  `click` waits for the presenter and starts a new subslide.
- Each animation takes `run-time:` (seconds) and `rate:` (easing).

```typst
#import "/lib.typ": *   // the touying checkout with scenes (rule 5)
#import themes.simple: *
#show: simple-theme.with(aspect-ratio: "16-9")
#let sc = touying-scene

== Energy

#sc.scene(
  width: 20cm,
  height: 6cm,
  objects: (
    eq: sc.obj(at: (10, 4), $E = m c^2$),
    note: sc.obj(at: (10, 2), text(size: 0.8em)[mass is energy]),
  ),
  timeline: (
    sc.write("eq"),
    sc.click,
    sc.play(sc.fade-in("note", shift: (0, -0.5)), sc.indicate("eq")),
  ),
)

#pause
Text after the scene appears on the page after the scene's last step.
```

### The scene

`scene(width:, height:, objects:, timeline:, id: auto, bounds: auto, unit: auto, cetz: none, camera: none, alt:
none, handout: auto, clip: false)`

- `width` and `height` are required lengths.
- **Coordinates.** Numbers are scene units, y up, with the origin at the bottom-left. By default one unit is 1 cm, so
  a `20cm × 6cm` scene spans x 0..20 and y 0..6. `bounds: ((xmin, ymin), (xmax, ymax))` sets another range, which
  is centred and widened to fill the box.
- `id` must be unique per slide when a slide has two scenes.
- `cetz: cetz` is needed for `cetz-obj`.
- `handout` is the state shown in handout and article mode: `auto` (the end), a segment number, or `"start"`.
- `alt` is text for screen readers in the HTML export.
- A scene must be at the top level of a slide body, not inside `only`, `uncover` or `alternatives`. Put `#pause`
  before it to reveal it later.

### Objects

| Constructor | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `obj(body, at: (0, 0), anchor: center + horizon)` | Any content (text, equation, image, table). `anchor` is the point of the object placed at `at`. |
| `cetz-obj(body)` | CeTZ draw commands in scene coordinates (needs `scene(cetz: cetz)`); must stay inside the scene bounds. |
| `tracked(fn, ..values, interpolate: false)` | Value tracker: `fn(v)` receives a dictionary of the current values and returns an object. Animate the values with `set-value`. |
| `shape(paths:, labels:)`, `path(pts: ..)` | Native paths in scene coordinates. |
| `group(..objs)` | Several objects drawn and animated as one, e.g. as the result of `tracked`. |
| graph helpers | `axes`, `plot`, `dot`, `tangent`, ... (section 9) |
| `surround(of:)`, `brace(of:)` | Annotations (section 11) |
| 3D objects | `surface`, `curve3d`, ... (section 12) |

Common options on every object:
- `visible: auto` hides an object at the start if its first animation brings it in (`fade-in`, `create`, `write`,
  `add`, `show-passing-flash`, or being the target of a `transform`). Set `true` or `false` to override.
- `pivot: auto` is the centre for rotation and scaling.
- `behind: true` draws a 2D object behind the 3D layer.

### Timeline entries

| Entry | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `play(..anims, run-time: auto, rate: auto, lag-ratio: 0)` | Run together. `lag-ratio: 1` runs them one after another; 0.5 overlaps them by half. |
| `wait(seconds)` | Pause. |
| `click` | Wait for a click. This starts a new subslide; start the timeline with `click` to show the empty state first. |

### Animations

Every animation also takes `run-time:` and `rate:`.

| Animation | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `fade-in(id, shift: none)`, `fade-out(id, shift: none)` | Fade, optionally moving by a vector `(dx, dy)`. |
| `create(id)`, `uncreate(id)` | Draw strokes progressively (other parts fade). |
| `write(id)`, `unwrite(id)` | Reveal from left to right (text, equations). |
| `add(id)`, `remove(id)` | Show or hide instantly. |
| `shift(id, (dx, dy))` | Move by a vector. |
| `move-to(id, (x, y))` | Move the anchor (the pivot for drawings) to a point. |
| `move-along(id, path)` | Follow an array of points or a function `t => (x, y)` on [0, 1]. |
| `rotate-by(id, angle)`, `scale-by(id, factor)` | Rotate (counter-clockwise) or scale about the pivot. |
| `indicate(id, scale: 1.2)` | Briefly enlarge. |
| `set-value(id, name: value, ..)` | Animate the values of a `tracked` object. |
| `transform(a, b, mode: auto)` | Morph `a` into `b`; `a` is gone afterwards (section 10). |
| `transform-matching(a, b)` | Rearrange an equation symbol by symbol (section 10). |
| `circumscribe`, `flash`, `focus-on`, `show-passing-flash`, `wiggle` | Emphasis (section 11). |
| `move-camera`, `rotate-camera`, `rotate-3d`, `shift-3d` | 3D (section 12). |

**Rates:** `"smooth"` (the default), `"linear"`, `"rush-into"`, `"rush-from"`, `"there-and-back"`,
`"ease-in-quad"`, `"ease-out-quad"`, `"ease-in-cubic"`, `"ease-out-cubic"`, `"ease-in-out-cubic"`,
`"ease-in-out-sine"`, or any function `t => ..` on [0, 1].

**Rules:**
- Two animations may not change the same property of the same object at the same time (e.g. two `shift`s of `"a"`
  in one `play`). Run them one after another.
- `create` and `show-passing-flash` on the same object may not overlap.
- Times in `wait`, `run-time` and `lag-ratio` are plain numbers.

### Value trackers

```typst
#import "/lib.typ": *
#import themes.simple: *
#show: simple-theme.with(aspect-ratio: "16-9", config-scene(samples-per-second: 12))
#let sc = touying-scene

== A growing circle

#sc.scene(
  width: 16cm,
  height: 6cm,
  objects: (
    c: sc.tracked(r: 0.5, interpolate: true, v => sc.obj(
      at: (8, 3),
      circle(radius: v.r * 1cm, fill: blue.lighten(60%)),
    )),
    label: sc.tracked(r: 0.5, v => sc.obj(at: (14, 3), $r = #calc.round(v.r, digits: 2)$)),
  ),
  timeline: (
    sc.click,
    sc.play(sc.set-value("c", r: 2.5), sc.set-value("label", r: 2.5), run-time: 2),
  ),
)
```

- In HTML, tracked objects are re-rendered by Typst at `config-scene(samples-per-second: ..)` (default 30).
- With `interpolate: true` the player blends samples, so 10–12 per second look smooth. Use it only when the drawing
  changes continuously.
- Leave text that shows rounded numbers at `interpolate: false`, as `label` above does. Give such an object its own
  rate, `tracked(.., samples-per-second: 30)`, so the number updates often without making other trackers heavier.

## 9. Scenes: graphs

The graph helpers draw natively (no CeTZ) and are ordinary objects, so `create`, `fade-in`, `transform` and so on
work on them.

```typst
#import "/lib.typ": *
#import themes.simple: *
#show: simple-theme.with(aspect-ratio: "16-9", config-scene(samples-per-second: 12))
#let sc = touying-scene

#let f(x) = x * x * x - 3 * x
#let ax = sc.axes(x: (-2.5, 2.5, 1), y: (-3, 3, 1), at: (1, 0.5), size: (10, 6), labels: ($x$, $y$))

== Tangent along a cubic

#sc.scene(
  width: 20cm,
  height: 7cm,
  objects: (
    ax: ax,
    graph: sc.plot(ax, f),
    t: sc.tracked(x: -2, interpolate: true, v => sc.group(
      sc.tangent(ax, f, v.x, df: x => 3 * x * x - 3),
      sc.dot(ax, (v.x, f(v.x))),
    )),
    eq: sc.obj(at: (16, 5), $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$),
  ),
  timeline: (
    sc.play(sc.create("ax"), sc.create("graph"), sc.write("eq")),
    sc.fade-in("t"),
    sc.click,
    sc.set-value("t", x: 2, run-time: 3, rate: "linear"),
  ),
)
```

**Axes.** `axes(x: (min, max, step), y: (min, max, step), at: (x0, y0), size: (w, h), ..)`:
- `at` is the bottom-left corner of the plot rectangle and `size` its width and height, both in scene units.
- Each axis line lies at the other axis' 0 if it is in range, else at its edge.
- Options:
  - `ticks: true`;
  - `numbers: auto | none | (values) | ((value, content), ..) | (x: .., y: ..)`;
  - `labels: ($x$, $y$)`;
  - `tips: true`, `grid: false`;
  - `stroke`, `tick-size`, `tip-size`, `number-size`.
- A step may be left out: `x: (0, 10)` gives no ticks on that axis.
- `c2p(ax, (x, y))` converts axis coordinates to scene coordinates. Use it for `obj(at: ..)`, `move-to`,
  `flash((x, y))` and so on.

| Helper | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `plot(ax, f, domain: auto, samples: 128, discontinuities: (), stroke:, dash:)` | Graph of `f`, clipped to the plot rectangle. |
| `dot(ax, (x, y), radius: 2.5pt, fill: black)` | A dot. |
| `tangent(ax, f, x, length: 2, df: none)` | Tangent at `x`, `length` scene units long; `df` is the exact derivative (else a numeric one). |
| `secant(ax, f, x1, x2, length: auto, guides: false)` | Secant; `guides: true` adds Δx/Δy legs and labels. `x1 == x2` is an error. |
| `area(ax, f, domain: (a, b), g: none, fill:, neg-fill: auto)` | Region between `f` and `g` (default the x axis); parts with `f < g` use `neg-fill`. |
| `riemann(ax, f, domain:, n: 10, mode: "left" \| "right" \| "mid", fill:, neg-fill:)` | Riemann rectangles. |
| `v-line(ax, (x, y))`, `h-line(ax, (x, y))` | Dashed guides from the axes to a point. |
| `graph-path(ax, f, domain: auto)` | A path for `move-along("dot", graph-path(ax, f))`. |

Gaps and poles:
- `f` may return `none` where it is undefined: `x => if x < 0 { none } else { calc.sqrt(x) }`. A Typst error such
  as `calc.sqrt(-1)` cannot be caught, so guard it like that.
- `discontinuities: (0,)` splits the graph at those x values, and `f` is never evaluated there:
  `plot(ax, x => 1 / x, discontinuities: (0,))`.

Smooth tracked graphs:
- A `tracked` graph object with `interpolate: true` stays smooth as long as its number of parts stays the same.
- It changes when `samples` or `n` change, when the graph crosses a gap or the plot border, or when label text
  changes.
- Pass `n: int(v.n)` to `riemann` inside a tracker, and leave such trackers at `interpolate: false`.

## 10. Scenes: morphing

- `transform(a, b)`: in HTML the outline of `a` morphs point by point into `b` (manim's `ReplacementTransform`).
  - Examples: circle to square, one graph to another, `$x^2$` to `$sin x$`.
  - Parts without a partner grow from or shrink to a point. `a` is invisible afterwards. In PDF, `b` simply replaces
    `a`.
- `transform(a, b, mode: "fade")` crossfades while moving and scaling between the two boxes.
- `transform(a, b, mode: "shape")` is a compile error when the timeline rules out a morph. Use it to make sure.
- `transform` falls back to the crossfade automatically when:
  - either object is animated otherwise during the morph;
  - either object is not fully visible;
  - the rate does not start at 0 and end at 1, such as `"there-and-back"`;
  - images, gradients or dashed strokes are involved;
  - another object drawn between them overlaps.
- `transform-matching(a, b)` rearranges equations: equal glyphs move to their new places and the rest fades. Mark
  corresponding parts that change size with `key`:

```typst
#let n = touying-scene.key.with("n")
// in objects:
//   src: sc.obj(at: (5, 2), $#n[$n$] dot x$),
//   dst: sc.obj(at: (5, 2), $x^#n[$n$]$),
// in the timeline:
//   sc.transform-matching("src", "dst")
```

Use `transform-matching` to keep symbols, `transform` to change shapes, and `mode: "fade"` for unrelated content.
During either morph, the two objects may not be animated by anything else.

## 11. Scenes: emphasis and annotations

Annotations are persistent objects. They are visible in PDF too, and `create` draws them in:

- `surround(of: "eq", buff: 0.15, shape: "rect" | "circle", radius: 0pt, stroke:, fill: none)` draws a box or
  circle around another object.
- `brace(of: "eq", side: bottom | top | left | right, label: [..], gap: 0.15, size: 0.25)` draws a curly brace
  with an optional label.

They measure the target where it is laid out (with its initial values) and do not follow later moves. To highlight
part of an equation, make that part its own `obj` and annotate it.

Effects play in HTML only and leave nothing behind in PDF:

| Animation | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `circumscribe(id, shape: "rect", fade: false, time-width: 0.3)` | An outline runs around the object once. `fade: true` draws it, holds it and fades it out. |
| `flash(id or (x, y), lines: 12, radius: auto, line-length: 0.3)` | Lines burst outwards. |
| `focus-on(id or (x, y))` | A spotlight shrinks onto the target. |
| `show-passing-flash(id, time-width: 0.3)` | A highlight runs along the object's strokes; the object is invisible afterwards. Use it on a coloured copy of a curve. |
| `wiggle(id, scale: 1.1, angle: 3.6deg, n: 6)` | Rotate back and forth while briefly growing (rate: linear; a custom rate must start at 0 and end at 1). |
| `indicate(id, scale: 1.2)` | Briefly enlarge. |

Effects measure their target when they start. To outline an object after it moved, put the effect after the move.

```typst
#import "/lib.typ": *
#import themes.simple: *
#show: simple-theme.with(aspect-ratio: "16-9")
#let sc = touying-scene

== Emphasis

#sc.scene(
  width: 20cm,
  height: 6cm,
  objects: (
    eq: sc.obj(at: (7, 3.5), text(size: 28pt, $F = m a$)),
    br: sc.brace(of: "eq", label: [Newton's second law]),
    star: sc.obj(at: (15, 3), circle(radius: 0.4cm, fill: orange)),
  ),
  timeline: (
    sc.write("eq"),
    sc.circumscribe("eq"),
    sc.click,
    sc.create("br"),
    sc.play(sc.flash("star"), sc.wiggle("eq")),
  ),
)
```

## 12. Scenes: 3D

Give the scene a camera: `scene(camera: sc.camera(phi: 70deg, theta: -45deg, zoom: 1, focal: none))`.
- `phi` is the polar angle from +z (0° looks straight down) and `theta` the azimuth.
- `focal: none` is orthographic; a number gives perspective.

| 3D object | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `surface(f: (x, y) => z, x: (a, b), y: (c, d), samples: (24, 24), fill:, stroke:, shade: false)` | Height field; `fill` may be a gradient (by height) or `(x, y, z) => color`. Parametric: `surface(fn: (u, v) => (x, y, z), u:, v:)`. |
| `curve3d(t => (x, y, z), t: (a, b), samples: 64)`, `line3d(..points, closed: false)` | Curves. |
| `vector3d(from, to)`, `point3d(p)`, `polygon3d(..points)` | Arrow, point, flat convex polygon. |
| `axes3d(x: (a, b), y:, z:, labels: ($x$, $y$, $z$))` | Axes. |
| `label3d(p, body, depth: false)` | Content at a 3D point, facing the viewer. |
| `group3d(..objects)` | Animate several as one. |

Animations:
- Camera: `move-camera(phi:, theta:, zoom:, focal:, center:)` and `rotate-camera(by: 360deg)` (an orbit, rate
  linear).
- Objects: `rotate-3d(id, angle, axis: "x" | "y" | "z" | (ax, ay, az), about: auto)` and `shift-3d(id, (dx, dy,
  dz))`, plus `fade-in`/`fade-out`/`add`/`remove`/`create`/`set-value`.
- 2D animations such as `shift` and `transform` are compile errors on 3D objects.
- Angles are literal: going from 350° to 10° turns back by 340°.
- 2D objects in the same scene are drawn in front of the 3D layer (or behind it with `behind: true`). Use them for
  formulas and captions.
- A `tracked` object may return a 3D object, for example a deforming surface. Its number of points must not change
  with the values.
- In HTML the audience can drag to look around, use the wheel to zoom and press <kbd>0</kbd> to reset; the next
  click turns the view back smoothly.

```typst
#import "/lib.typ": *
#import themes.simple: *
#show: simple-theme.with(aspect-ratio: "16-9")
#let sc = touying-scene

== A saddle

#sc.scene(
  width: 20cm,
  height: 8cm,
  camera: sc.camera(phi: 65deg, theta: -50deg, zoom: 1.2),
  objects: (
    axes: sc.axes3d(x: (-2.5, 2.5), y: (-2.5, 2.5), z: (-2, 2)),
    surf: sc.surface(
      f: (x, y) => (x * x - y * y) / 4,
      x: (-2, 2),
      y: (-2, 2),
      samples: (16, 16),
      fill: gradient.linear(..color.map.viridis),
      shade: true,
    ),
    eq: sc.obj(at: (0.5cm, 0.5cm), anchor: left + top, $z = (x^2 - y^2) / 4$),
  ),
  timeline: (
    sc.play(sc.create("axes"), sc.fade-in("surf"), sc.fade-in("eq")),
    sc.click,
    sc.rotate-camera(by: 90deg, run-time: 3),
  ),
)
```

## 13. HTML export

touying-exporter is the `dependencies/touying-exporter` submodule of the touying checkout; install it with
`pip install -e dependencies/touying-exporter`.

```sh
touying compile slides.typ --root .          # writes slides.html (animated scenes)
typst compile slides.typ --root .            # PDF: one page per step
typst compile slides.typ --root . --input export-mode=handout handout.pdf
```

- The HTML is one compressed, self-contained file that works offline.
- Keys:
  - <kbd>→</kbd>, <kbd>Space</kbd> or a click: next. During an animation, the first press finishes it.
  - <kbd>←</kbd>: back. <kbd>R</kbd>: replay. <kbd>F</kbd>: fullscreen. <kbd>N</kbd>: notes.
  - <kbd>P</kbd> or <kbd>S</kbd>: presenter window with the current and next page, notes and a timer.
- To inspect what the player receives:
  `typst eval 'query(<touying-scene>).map(e => e.value)' --in slides.typ --input touying-scene=html`.

## 14. Errors and fixes

| Message (excerpt) | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `overlapping animations on \`x\` (tx)` | Two animations change the same property at the same time. Use separate `play`s, or animate different properties. |
| `overlapping animations on \`x\` (dash)` | `create` and `show-passing-flash` overlap on one object. Run them one after another. |
| `unknown object \`x\`` | A timeline entry or `of:` names an object that is not in `objects`. |
| `object name ... may only contain letters, digits` | Rename the object (no spaces or dots). |
| `cetz object ... draws outside the scene bounds` | Enlarge `bounds`, or keep the drawing inside. |
| `cetz-obj needs the cetz module` | Pass `scene(cetz: cetz)` after `#import "@preview/cetz:0.5.2"`. |
| `does not apply to the 3D object` | Use the 3D animations (`rotate-3d`, `shift-3d`) on 3D objects. |
| `needs scene(camera: camera(..))` | Add a camera to scenes with 3D objects. |
| `mode: "shape"` ... | That morph cannot happen because of the timeline. Remove the concurrent animation, or use `mode: auto`. |
| `secant: x1 and x2 are equal` | Use `tangent` for the limit. |
| `the rate must start at 0 and end at 1` | `wiggle`, `transform-matching` and shape morphs need such a rate (not `"there-and-back"`). |
| `tracked object ... needs N samples` | Lower `config-scene(samples-per-second: ..)`, raise `max-samples`, or use `interpolate: true` with fewer samples. |
| `Unsupported mark` / `pause` inside a function | Use the callback style `slide(repeat: n, self => ..)`, or move the marker out of the function call. |
| A scene inside `only`/`uncover` fails | Put scenes at the top level of a slide body; use `#pause` before them. |
| `unknown variable: touying-scene` | You imported the released `@preview/touying:0.8.1`; import the checkout with scenes (rule 5). |

## 15. Checklist before handing a deck over

1. `typst compile` succeeds without errors.
2. Render a few pages to PNG and look at them: nothing overflows the slide, and text sizes are readable.
3. Scenes: every `click` is intended (each adds a PDF page), objects that should appear later have intro animations
   or `visible: false`, and the last state is meaningful in PDF.
4. For HTML, run `touying compile` and open the file. Check that animations run, and that morphs look as intended
   (`transform` vs `transform-matching`).
5. Speaker notes are in `#speaker-note[..]`, not on the slides.
